{{Probability distribution|name=''κ''-Logistic distribution|type=density|parameters=<math> 0 \leq \kappa < 1 </math>  <br /> <math> \alpha > 0 </math> [[shape parameter|shape]] ([[Real number|real]]) <br /> <math> \beta> 0 </math> [[rate parameter|rate]] ([[Real number|real]])  <br /> <math>  \lambda > 0  </math>|support=<math>x \in [0, \infty)</math>|pdf=<math> \frac{\lambda \alpha \beta x^{\alpha-1} }{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 \beta^2 x^{2\alpha} } } \frac{ \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) }{ [ 1 + (\lambda - 1) \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha)]^2 } </math>|cdf=<math>\frac{ 1 - \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) }{  1 + (\lambda - 1) \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) }</math>|cdf_image=FILE:Kaniadakis logistic Distribution cdf.png|pdf_image=FILE:Kaniadakis logistic Distribution pdf.png|pdf_caption=Plot of the κ-Logistic distribution for typical κ-values and <math> \beta = 1 </math>. The case <math> \kappa = 0 </math> corresponds to the ordinary Logistic distribution.|cdf_caption=Plots of the cumulative κ-Logistic distribution for typical κ-values and <math> \beta = 1 </math>. The case <math> \kappa = 0 </math> corresponds to the ordinary Logistic case.}}The '''Kaniadakis Logistic distribution''' (also known as '''''κ-''Logisticdistribution)''' is a generalized version of the [[Logistic distribution]] associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics]].  It is one example of a [[Kaniadakis distribution]]. The κ-Logistic probability distribution describes the population kinetics behavior of bosonic (<math>0 < \lambda < 1</math>) or fermionic (<math> \lambda > 1</math>) character.<ref name=":0" />

== Definitions ==

=== Probability density function ===
The Kaniadakis ''κ''-Logistic distribution is a four-parameter family of [[Probability distribution|continuous statistical distributions]], which is part of a class of [[statistical distributions]] emerging from the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis κ-statistics]]. This distribution has the following [[probability density function]]:<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2021-01-01 |title=New power-law tailed distributions emerging in κ-statistics (a) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=133 |issue=1 |article-number=10002 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/133/10002 |issn=0295-5075|arxiv=2203.01743 |bibcode=2021EL....13310002K |s2cid=234144356 }}</ref>

: <math> 
f_{_{\kappa}}(x) = 
\frac{\lambda \alpha \beta x^{\alpha-1}}{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 \beta^2 x^{2\alpha} }} \frac{ \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) }{ [ 1 + (\lambda - 1) \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha)]^2 }
</math>

valid for  <math>x \geq 0</math>,  where <math>0 \leq |\kappa| < 1</math> is the entropic index associated with the [[Kaniadakis statistics|Kaniadakis entropy]], <math>\beta > 0</math> is the [[rate parameter]], <math>\lambda > 0</math>, and <math>\alpha > 0</math> is the shape parameter.

The [[Logistic distribution]] is recovered as <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0.</math>

=== Cumulative distribution function ===
The [[cumulative distribution function]] of ''κ''-Logistic is given by

: <math>F_\kappa(x) = 
\frac{ 1 - \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) }{  1 + (\lambda - 1) \exp_\kappa(-\beta x^\alpha) } </math>

valid for  <math>x \geq 0</math>. The cumulative Logistic distribution is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

=== Survival and hazard functions ===
The survival distribution function of ''κ''-Logistic distribution is given by

: <math>S_\kappa(x) = 
\frac{\lambda}{\exp_\kappa(\beta x^\alpha) + \lambda - 1}</math>

valid for  <math>x \geq 0</math>. The survival [[Logistic distribution]] is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

The hazard function associated with the ''κ''-Logistic distribution is obtained by the solution of the following evolution equation:<blockquote><math>\frac{ S_\kappa(x) }{ dx } = -h_\kappa S_\kappa(x) \left( 1 - \frac{ \lambda -1 }{ \lambda } S_\kappa(x)  \right)  </math></blockquote>with  <math>S_\kappa(0) = 1</math>, where  <math>h_\kappa</math> is the hazard function:

:<math>h_\kappa = \frac{\alpha \beta x^{\alpha-1}}{\sqrt{1+\kappa^2 \beta^2 x^{2\alpha} }}  </math>

The cumulative Kaniadakis ''κ''-Logistic distribution is related to the hazard function by the following expression:

:<math>S_\kappa = e^{-H_\kappa(x)}  </math>

where <math>H_\kappa (x) = \int_0^x h_\kappa(z) dz  </math> is the cumulative hazard function. The cumulative hazard function of the [[Logistic distribution]] is recovered in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.

==Related distributions==
*The survival function of the ''κ''-Logistic distribution represents the ''κ''-deformation of the Fermi-Dirac function, and becomes a [[Fermi-Dirac distribution]] in the classical limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.<ref name=":0" />
*The ''κ''-Logistic distribution is a generalization of the [[Kaniadakis Weibull distribution|''κ''-Weibull distribution]] when <math>\lambda = 1</math>.
*A ''κ''-Logistic distribution corresponds to a [[Half-logistic distribution|Half-Logistic distribution]] when <math>\lambda = 2</math>, <math>\alpha = 1</math> and <math>\kappa = 0</math>.
*The ordinary Logistic distribution is a particular case of a ''κ''-Logistic distribution, when <math>\kappa = 0</math>.

== Applications ==
The ''κ''-Logistic distribution has been applied in several areas, such as:

* In [[quantum statistics]], the survival function of the ''κ''-Logistic distribution represents the most general expression of the Fermi-Dirac function, reducing to the [[Fermi-Dirac distribution]] in the limit <math>\kappa \rightarrow 0</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Santos |first1=A.P. |last2=Silva |first2=R. |last3=Alcaniz |first3=J.S. |last4=Anselmo |first4=D.H.A.L. |date=2011 |title=Kaniadakis statistics and the quantum H-theorem |journal=Physics Letters A |language=en |volume=375 |issue=3 |pages=352–355 |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2010.11.045|bibcode=2011PhLA..375..352S |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kaniadakis |first=G. |date=2001 |title=H-theorem and generalized entropies within the framework of nonlinear kinetics |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0375960101005436 |journal=Physics Letters A |language=en |volume=288 |issue=5–6 |pages=283–291 |doi=10.1016/S0375-9601(01)00543-6|arxiv=cond-mat/0109192 |bibcode=2001PhLA..288..283K |s2cid=119445915 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lourek |first1=Imene |last2=Tribeche |first2=Mouloud |date=2017 |title=Thermodynamic properties of the blackbody radiation: A Kaniadakis approach |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0375960116320060 |journal=Physics Letters A |language=en |volume=381 |issue=5 |pages=452–456 |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2016.12.019|bibcode=2017PhLA..381..452L |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
